conv_126.speaker: xX_Crumbwright_Xx
conv_126.text: Good evening. I have been considering a raid on {village}, and I think our forces could manage it together.

conv_126.speaker: OldCloakwright
conv_126.text: Sit a while, Crumbwright. A joint raid is a fine notion, but I will want to see your men before I promise anything.

conv_126.speaker: xX_Crumbwright_Xx
conv_126.text: Naturally. I can bring {troop_count} riders from the salt roads. Would you trust my word on the division of spoils?

conv_126.speaker: OldCloakwright
conv_126.text: I trust a man's word less than his horses. Still, {gold} in plunder is not a sum to sneer at. Name your terms.

conv_126.speaker: xX_Crumbwright_Xx
conv_126.text: Interesting. You were not at {town} when the last caravan fell, were you? I wonder why you are so eager now.

conv_126.speaker: OldCloakwright
conv_126.text: Let us not dig up old graves tonight. Send me your muster list, and we shall see whether your word is worth more than mine.

conv_126.speaker: xX_Crumbwright_Xx
conv_126.text: Fair enough. My muster list will reach you by morning, and I expect your riders at the ford before dawn.

conv_127.speaker: TurnipTheFlank
conv_127.text: honour is a word losers use after they lose. the scoreboard does not remember who was polite

conv_127.speaker: Cobbled_Envoy
conv_127.text: Shall we discuss this over wine, Turnip? A reputation outlasts any single battle, and yours is worth more than you think.

conv_127.speaker: hensworn
conv_127.text: Sit down Turnip. The road will wait. Honour buys nothing at the gate but it keeps the men who follow you.

conv_127.speaker: TurnipTheFlank
conv_127.text: men who follow for honour leave when a better offer shows up. ive watched it happen 300 times

conv_127.speaker: Cobbled_Envoy
conv_127.text: Then you have not seen men who follow a leader they trust. Loyalty and honour are not enemies, Turnip.

conv_127.speaker: hensworn
conv_127.text: Trust is slow to build and quick to spend. Winning gets you a crowd. Honour gets you a few friends who stay.

conv_127.speaker: TurnipTheFlank
conv_127.text: a crowd is just friends who have not been offered {gold} yet

conv_128.speaker: xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx
conv_128.text: Bandits on the {village} road again. Terrible for trade. Half my wagons are sitting idle in {town}.

conv_128.speaker: Brakken_Mouthy
conv_128.text: lol ottr ur stil salty abuot the tollhouse thing. nobdy cares abt ur wagons

conv_128.speaker: Dovran_Oatsworn
conv_128.text: Please, Brakken. The road has enough grief without your jokes. I am weary of hearing it mocked.

conv_128.speaker: xX_Fiddl3Kid_Xx
conv_128.text: lol still laughing at the tollhouse brakken. u paid the toll and then cried about it

conv_128.speaker: Brakken_Mouthy
conv_128.text: fiddl3 shut up ur from tsevaret. ur whole faction been losing favour since spring

conv_128.speaker: xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx
conv_128.text: Losing favour is a fact of politics. The Wardenry has seen its share of shifts, and I would rather talk about prices.

conv_128.speaker: Dovran_Oatsworn
conv_128.text: Gossip spreads faster than grain in a dry year. Mind your tongues before someone takes it to the wardens.

conv_128.speaker: xX_Fiddl3Kid_Xx
conv_128.text: lol the wardens dont scare me. they cry about {village} while i count my coin

conv_129.speaker: spindly_knight
conv_129.text: Hi! Um, are you the one recruiting for the {town} campaign? I was told to ask you :) Sorry if I am bothering you!!

conv_129.speaker: Glovaric_Ironhand
conv_129.text: Hear this: the glove shall not yield at {village}. I recruit only those who can hold a line under fire.

conv_129.speaker: spindly_knight
conv_129.text: Oh!! I can hold a line :) I think. I have {troop_count} men and a few good shields. Did I say that right? :D

conv_129.speaker: Glovaric_Ironhand
conv_129.text: Your shields matter little to me. Discipline wins where enthusiasm fails. Prove yours and we shall speak further.

conv_129.speaker: spindly_knight
conv_129.text: Oh okay!! I can do discipline :) Um, are you the knight who won at {village} last spring? That was so cool!

conv_129.speaker: Glovaric_Ironhand
conv_129.text: I am. Do not mistake courtesy for friendship, young one. Arrive at the muster with {gold} in supplies or do not arrive at all.

conv_129.speaker: spindly_knight
conv_129.text: Right!! I will bring {gold} :) Sorry if I was annoying. Thank you for hearing me out!

conv_130.speaker: SerTankardell
conv_130.text: Hark! Tesnovar's oath still binds us all, and I call upon every honest blade to ride beside me against the tyranny of {town}.

conv_130.speaker: rustcouncil07
conv_130.text: a quiet word, SerTankardell? just between us. oaths sound lovely but {gold} pays for swords and i hear ur short of both

conv_130.speaker: SerTankardell
conv_130.text: Sir, I am no man's purse. Tesnovar's banners are not for sale, and I would think you would know better than to ask.

conv_130.speaker: rustcouncil07
conv_130.text: everyones for sale at some price. even knights. i just pay quicker than the council does. think on it, ok

conv_130.speaker: SerTankardell
conv_130.text: I have thought on it, and the answer is no. Tesnovar stands unbought and unafraid of your {troop_count} hired blades.

conv_130.speaker: rustcouncil07
conv_130.text: brave words from a man who has never been paid. ok fine ill leave ur oath alone. offer stays open tho, til {town} falls

conv_130.speaker: SerTankardell
conv_130.text: Then let your offer rot, sir, and let the oath be my only currency. We march at dawn, with or without your gold.
